body:
## Problem:
`vim.fs.slug()` does not handle URIs like `term://foo//123:bash`,
so callers (e.g. terminal persistence) must strip the scheme before
calling `slug()`.

## Solution:
Detect `scheme://` from the raw input before `normalize()` and
replace it with a `=uri-<scheme>-` prefix.

comment_data.body:
This is unfortunately a bad example: `~` is not expanded, so `vim.fs.slug('term://~/proj//123:bash')` is equivalent to `vim.fs.slug('term://./~/proj//123:bash')`, not `vim.fs.slug('term:///home/username/proj//123:bash')`.

I understand that this is just how `term://` works, so when you get around to using `vim.fs.slug()` for `term://`, you're either going to need to change the term URI to expand "\~", or manually expand "\~" before passing it to `vim.fs.slug()`.

> you're either going to need to change the term URI to expand "~", or manually expand "~" before passing it to `vim.fs.slug()`.

why? that is the reverse of how we treat `$HOME` in a normal path.

Two reasons:
1. We're using `opts.plain = true` when calling `vim.fs.normalize()`.
2. Even if we were using `opts.plain = false`, `vim.fs.normalize()` only expands "\~" when it is a leading character, and since all URIs will be prefixed by `{scheme}://`, the "\~" is never leading.
why do we want to expand it? `slug()` un-expands it when it is at the start, but won't be able to do so in a `term:` URI. why don't we just leave "~" as-is in a term URI.
Oh, I see what you mean. Because the hash will be different.

> `vim.fs.slug('term://~/proj//123:bash')` is equivalent to `vim.fs.slug('term://./~/proj//123:bash')`

eh... that's something `:terminal` needs to be fix. if slug() tries to workaround that then we have 2 problems.

> Because the hash will be different.

if you are referring to hash collisions for "~"  for 2 different users, that's fine. these are per-user, private slugs.
Mhm. I'm just saying that makes `term://` a bad example imo. And yes, that's for `:terminal` to fix, I agree.

> This is unfortunately a bad example: `~` is not expanded, so `vim.fs.slug('term://~/proj//123:bash')` is equivalent to `vim.fs.slug('term://./~/proj//123:bash')`, not `vim.fs.slug('term:///home/username/proj//123:bash')`.

I think this example is fine. `term://` URI guarantees that `$HOME` -> `~` and no `./`, `../` in there. So `slug()` will never actually encounter `term://./~/proj//123:bash` or `term:///home/username/proj//123:bash`, well, unless users change it.

> that's something `:terminal` needs to be fix.

> And yes, that's for `:terminal` to fix, I agree.

fix what? making the `cwd` in terminal URI an absolute path?

> `term://` URI guarantees that `$HOME` -> `~` and no `./`, `../` in there.

I understand that's how `term://` works, but the average person doesn't, making it a bad example. I also think that's a property of `term://` that should be fixed....

> fix what?

Fix "\~" being in the terminal URI. Not exactly a bug, because as you mentioned, there's no chance of collision with a literal directory named "\~", but because it not being expanded is unideal (imo). Either way, this probably isn't the place to discuss changes to `term://`; I'd just prefer a different example if possible.
